baseline_rationale: Measles is a highly contagious disease, but vaccination rates in the U.S. are generally high, which significantly reduces the likelihood of outbreaks and associated deaths. Given the effectiveness of the measles vaccine and the public health measures in place, it is reasonable to predict that the majority of the time, there will be no reported deaths. A small number of deaths could occur in unvaccinated populations, but these would likely be limited.
